description: Two laps on the shared 10 m distance grid: where the time went, and how certain each figure is. Provisioned from servicios/grafana/provisioning/dashboards/json/pit-wall/pit-wall.json — edits made here are overwritten from disk.

panels.title: Lap A — $driver_a
panels.description: Official lap time from the timing feed (F002), not a figure this pipeline computed.

targets.rawSql: SELECT lap_time_s FROM dim_lap WHERE lap_id = $lap_a

panels.title: Lap B — $driver_b
panels.description: Official lap time from the timing feed (F002), not a figure this pipeline computed.

targets.rawSql: SELECT lap_time_s FROM dim_lap WHERE lap_id = $lap_b

panels.title: Official gap (B − A)
panels.description: The difference of the two official lap times. The panel to the right is what this pipeline reconstructs from telemetry; the two should agree to within the F010 residual.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT b.lap_time_s - a.lap_time_s AS gap_s
FROM dim_lap a
JOIN dim_lap b ON b.lap_id = $lap_b
WHERE a.lap_id = $lap_a

panels.title: Reconstructed gap at the last shared grid point
panels.description: Δt where the two laps stop sharing grid points. It is measured on the 10 m grid from each lap's own start, so it will not match the official gap exactly — F010 measured that residual at p50 0.054 s, p95 0.147 s.

targets.rawSql:
WITH s AS (
    SELECT season, round, session_code FROM dim_session WHERE session_id = $session
)
SELECT b.t_s - a.t_s AS delta_end_s
FROM fact_telemetry_grid a
JOIN s ON a.season = s.season AND a.round = s.round AND a.session_code = s.session_code
JOIN fact_telemetry_grid b
  ON b.season = s.season AND b.round = s.round AND b.session_code = s.session_code
 AND b.lap_id = $lap_b
 AND b.grid_index = a.grid_index
WHERE a.lap_id = $lap_a
ORDER BY a.grid_index DESC
LIMIT 1

panels.title: Tyres and reconstruction residual
panels.description: 'thin start' and 'thin end' flag a lap whose telemetry was sparse at the timing line (F010): read its Δt ends with that in mind.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT CASE WHEN lap_id = $lap_a THEN 'A' ELSE 'B' END AS side,
       code           AS driver,
       lap_number     AS lap,
       compound,
       stint,
       tyre_life      AS "tyre life",
       lap_time_s     AS "lap time s",
       lap_residual_s AS "grid − official s",
       start_coverage_poor AS "thin start",
       end_coverage_poor   AS "thin end"
FROM dim_lap
WHERE lap_id IN ($lap_a, $lap_b)
ORDER BY side

panels.title: Pit wall — hover to read every channel at one distance
$driver_a (A) vs $driver_b (B) — Δt, speed, throttle and brake against distance
panels.description: One panel, because Grafana's Trend visualisation has no shared crosshair: hovering here reads every channel at the same distance, which stacked panels cannot do. Δt is on the left axis, speed on the right; throttle and brake share a hidden axis. Δt rising means B is losing time.

targets.rawSql:
WITH s AS (
    SELECT season, round, session_code FROM dim_session WHERE session_id = $session
)
SELECT a.distance_m         AS distance_m,
       b.t_s - a.t_s        AS "Δt (B−A)",
       a.speed              AS "speed A",
       b.speed              AS "speed B",
       a.throttle           AS "throttle A",
       b.throttle           AS "throttle B",
       a.brake::int         AS "brake A",
       b.brake::int         AS "brake B"
FROM fact_telemetry_grid a
JOIN s ON a.season = s.season AND a.round = s.round AND a.session_code = s.session_code
JOIN fact_telemetry_grid b
  ON b.season = s.season AND b.round = s.round AND b.session_code = s.session_code
 AND b.lap_id = $lap_b
 AND b.grid_index = a.grid_index
WHERE a.lap_id = $lap_a
ORDER BY a.grid_index

panels.title: Speed
panels.description: A blue, B orange. Read on the 10 m grid, so a corner minimum here is the lowest speed over a 10 m window rather than an instantaneous one — the corner table applies the same caveat to V_min (D6).

targets.rawSql:
WITH s AS (
    SELECT season, round, session_code FROM dim_session WHERE session_id = $session
)
SELECT a.distance_m AS distance_m,
       a.speed AS "A",
       b.speed AS "B"
FROM fact_telemetry_grid a
JOIN s ON a.season = s.season AND a.round = s.round AND a.session_code = s.session_code
JOIN fact_telemetry_grid b
  ON b.season = s.season AND b.round = s.round AND b.session_code = s.session_code
 AND b.lap_id = $lap_b
 AND b.grid_index = a.grid_index
WHERE a.lap_id = $lap_a
ORDER BY a.grid_index

panels.title: Throttle
panels.description: A continuous channel, so it is interpolated between samples — unlike brake, gear and DRS below.

targets.rawSql:
WITH s AS (
    SELECT season, round, session_code FROM dim_session WHERE session_id = $session
)
SELECT a.distance_m AS distance_m,
       a.throttle AS "A",
       b.throttle AS "B"
FROM fact_telemetry_grid a
JOIN s ON a.season = s.season AND a.round = s.round AND a.session_code = s.session_code
JOIN fact_telemetry_grid b
  ON b.season = s.season AND b.round = s.round AND b.session_code = s.session_code
 AND b.lap_id = $lap_b
 AND b.grid_index = a.grid_index
WHERE a.lap_id = $lap_a
ORDER BY a.grid_index

panels.title: Brake
panels.description: A flag, drawn as a step: it is never interpolated between samples.

targets.rawSql:
WITH s AS (
    SELECT season, round, session_code FROM dim_session WHERE session_id = $session
)
SELECT a.distance_m AS distance_m,
       a.brake::int AS "A",
       b.brake::int AS "B"
FROM fact_telemetry_grid a
JOIN s ON a.season = s.season AND a.round = s.round AND a.session_code = s.session_code
JOIN fact_telemetry_grid b
  ON b.season = s.season AND b.round = s.round AND b.session_code = s.session_code
 AND b.lap_id = $lap_b
 AND b.grid_index = a.grid_index
WHERE a.lap_id = $lap_a
ORDER BY a.grid_index

panels.title: Gear
panels.description: A discrete channel, drawn as a step: it is never interpolated between samples.

targets.rawSql:
WITH s AS (
    SELECT season, round, session_code FROM dim_session WHERE session_id = $session
)
SELECT a.distance_m AS distance_m,
       a.n_gear AS "A",
       b.n_gear AS "B"
FROM fact_telemetry_grid a
JOIN s ON a.season = s.season AND a.round = s.round AND a.session_code = s.session_code
JOIN fact_telemetry_grid b
  ON b.season = s.season AND b.round = s.round AND b.session_code = s.session_code
 AND b.lap_id = $lap_b
 AND b.grid_index = a.grid_index
WHERE a.lap_id = $lap_a
ORDER BY a.grid_index

panels.title: DRS
panels.description: FastF1's raw DRS code, drawn as a step: it is never interpolated. 8, 10, 12 and 14 mean the flap is open.

targets.rawSql:
WITH s AS (
    SELECT season, round, session_code FROM dim_session WHERE session_id = $session
)
SELECT a.distance_m AS distance_m,
       a.drs AS "A",
       b.drs AS "B"
FROM fact_telemetry_grid a
JOIN s ON a.season = s.season AND a.round = s.round AND a.session_code = s.session_code
JOIN fact_telemetry_grid b
  ON b.season = s.season AND b.round = s.round AND b.session_code = s.session_code
 AND b.lap_id = $lap_b
 AND b.grid_index = a.grid_index
WHERE a.lap_id = $lap_a
ORDER BY a.grid_index

panels.title: Micro-sector loss, B − A — above zero is time B lost
panels.description: Corner-phase micro-sectors (F009) in track order. A sector shorter than $min_sector_m m is noise on its own (F004), so it is not given its own bar — but the short ones are pooled into the last bar rather than dropped, because on a close pair of laps they can carry as much delta as the ranked ones. What is drawn therefore adds up to the Δt at the end of the last complete sector.

targets.rawSql:
WITH s AS (
    SELECT season, round, session_code FROM dim_session WHERE session_id = $session
)
SELECT sector, "Δ B−A"
FROM (
    SELECT '#' || d.microsector_id || '  ' || coalesce(nullif(d.corners, ''), 'straight') || '  ·  ' || d.phase AS sector,
           fb.time_s - fa.time_s AS "Δ B−A",
           d.microsector_id AS ord
    FROM dim_microsector d
    CROSS JOIN s
    JOIN fact_microsector fa
      ON fa.season = s.season AND fa.round = s.round AND fa.session_code = s.session_code
     AND fa.lap_id = $lap_a AND fa.grain = d.grain AND fa.microsector_id = d.microsector_id
    JOIN fact_microsector fb
      ON fb.season = s.season AND fb.round = s.round AND fb.session_code = s.session_code
     AND fb.lap_id = $lap_b AND fb.grain = d.grain AND fb.microsector_id = d.microsector_id
    WHERE d.session_id = $session
      AND d.grain = 'corner_phase'
      AND d.length_m >= $min_sector_m
      AND NOT fa.partial
      AND NOT fb.partial

    UNION ALL

    SELECT 'under ' || $min_sector_m || ' m  ·  ' || count(*) || ' sectors pooled',
           sum(fb.time_s - fa.time_s),
           1000000
    FROM dim_microsector d
    CROSS JOIN s
    JOIN fact_microsector fa
      ON fa.season = s.season AND fa.round = s.round AND fa.session_code = s.session_code
     AND fa.lap_id = $lap_a AND fa.grain = d.grain AND fa.microsector_id = d.microsector_id
    JOIN fact_microsector fb
      ON fb.season = s.season AND fb.round = s.round AND fb.session_code = s.session_code
     AND fb.lap_id = $lap_b AND fb.grain = d.grain AND fb.microsector_id = d.microsector_id
    WHERE d.session_id = $session
      AND d.grain = 'corner_phase'
      AND d.length_m < $min_sector_m
      AND NOT fa.partial
      AND NOT fb.partial
    HAVING count(*) > 0
) ranked
ORDER BY ord

panels.title: Every micro-sector, including the short ones
panels.description: The footer sums the Δ column. Because these sectors partition the lap, that sum is the Δt at the end of the last complete sector — the closure F004 proved and the test asserts.

targets.rawSql:
WITH s AS (
    SELECT season, round, session_code FROM dim_session WHERE session_id = $session
)
SELECT d.microsector_id AS "#",
       coalesce(nullif(d.corners, ''), 'straight') AS corners,
       d.phase,
       d.start_m  AS "start m",
       d.length_m AS "length m",
       d.length_m >= $min_sector_m AS ranked,
       fa.time_s AS "A s",
       fb.time_s AS "B s",
       fb.time_s - fa.time_s AS "Δ B−A s"
FROM dim_microsector d
CROSS JOIN s
JOIN fact_microsector fa
  ON fa.season = s.season AND fa.round = s.round AND fa.session_code = s.session_code
 AND fa.lap_id = $lap_a AND fa.grain = d.grain AND fa.microsector_id = d.microsector_id
JOIN fact_microsector fb
  ON fb.season = s.season AND fb.round = s.round AND fb.session_code = s.session_code
 AND fb.lap_id = $lap_b AND fb.grain = d.grain AND fb.microsector_id = d.microsector_id
WHERE d.session_id = $session
  AND d.grain = 'corner_phase'
  AND NOT fa.partial
  AND NOT fb.partial
ORDER BY d.microsector_id

panels.title: Corners — minimum speed and braking point, with their uncertainty
Corner by corner
panels.description: Every speed-trough event F009 found, braked or not: the two blank braking rows are the events that carry no braking at all, which is why they are also marked marginal. Each braking point carries its own ±, the spacing of the two telemetry samples that bracket it (decision D6) — a braking point interpolated across a 40 m gap is not the same measurement as one taken between samples 8 m apart. The Δ brake column names the ± 20 m window below which a difference is not a difference.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT coalesce(nullif(e.corners, ''), 'event ' || e.event_id) AS corner,
       e.apex_m AS "apex m",
       ma.v_min_kmh AS "V_min A",
       mb.v_min_kmh AS "V_min B",
       mb.v_min_kmh - ma.v_min_kmh AS "ΔV_min",
       to_char(ma.brake_on_m::numeric, 'FM99990') || ' m ± '
         || to_char(ma.brake_gap_m::numeric, 'FM9990') || ' m' AS "brake A",
       to_char(mb.brake_on_m::numeric, 'FM99990') || ' m ± '
         || to_char(mb.brake_gap_m::numeric, 'FM9990') || ' m' AS "brake B",
       mb.brake_on_m - ma.brake_on_m AS "Δ brake m (D6: ± 20 m is not a difference)",
       e.marginal AS "marginal event"
FROM dim_corner_event e
JOIN fact_corner_metric ma ON ma.lap_id = $lap_a AND ma.event_id = e.event_id
JOIN fact_corner_metric mb ON mb.lap_id = $lap_b AND mb.event_id = e.event_id
WHERE e.session_id = $session
ORDER BY e.apex_m

panels.title: ΔV_min per corner, B − A — above zero is B carrying more speed
panels.description: Minimum speed is read from the 10 m grid, so it is a floor over a 10 m window rather than an instantaneous minimum (decision D6).

targets.rawSql:
SELECT coalesce(nullif(e.corners, ''), 'event ' || e.event_id) AS corner,
       mb.v_min_kmh - ma.v_min_kmh AS "ΔV_min"
FROM dim_corner_event e
JOIN fact_corner_metric ma ON ma.lap_id = $lap_a AND ma.event_id = e.event_id
JOIN fact_corner_metric mb ON mb.lap_id = $lap_b AND mb.event_id = e.event_id
WHERE e.session_id = $session
ORDER BY e.apex_m

panels.title: Every lap
panels.description: The whole session, quickest first. 'reference' marks the lap F004 used as the session default — the Δt stored in fact_telemetry_grid is against that lap, while this dashboard subtracts the two selected laps directly.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT code AS driver,
       lap_number AS lap,
       lap_time_s AS "lap time s",
       compound,
       stint,
       tyre_life AS "tyre life",
       lap_residual_s AS "grid − official s",
       is_reference AS reference
FROM dim_lap
WHERE session_id = $session
ORDER BY lap_time_s NULLS LAST

panels.title: Stint pace — $driver_a and $driver_b
panels.description: Seconds spent in each corner phase over a whole lap, averaged across the laps of a stint. Only laps carrying every sector of that phase are counted, so a lap that ended early cannot look quick — which is why the lap count differs by phase: most laps end inside a straight, so 'straight' is computed over fewer of them. Two drivers only, because stint numbers are per driver and pooling them across the field would compare unrelated things.

targets.rawSql:
WITH s AS (
    SELECT season, round, session_code FROM dim_session WHERE session_id = $session
),
sectors AS (
    SELECT microsector_id, phase
    FROM dim_microsector
    WHERE session_id = $session
      AND grain = 'corner_phase'
      AND length_m >= $min_sector_m
),
expected AS (
    SELECT phase, count(*) AS n_expected FROM sectors GROUP BY phase
),
per_lap AS (
    SELECT l.lap_id, l.code, l.compound, l.stint, sec.phase,
           sum(f.time_s) AS phase_time_s,
           count(*)      AS n_sectors
    FROM fact_microsector f
    CROSS JOIN s
    JOIN dim_lap l ON l.lap_id = f.lap_id
    JOIN sectors sec ON sec.microsector_id = f.microsector_id
    WHERE f.season = s.season AND f.round = s.round AND f.session_code = s.session_code
      AND f.grain = 'corner_phase'
      AND NOT f.partial
      AND f.time_s IS NOT NULL
      AND l.session_id = $session
    GROUP BY l.lap_id, l.code, l.compound, l.stint, sec.phase
)
SELECT p.code AS driver, p.compound, p.stint, p.phase,
       count(*) AS laps,
       avg(p.phase_time_s)          AS "mean s",
       stddev_samp(p.phase_time_s)  AS "std s"
FROM per_lap p
JOIN expected e ON e.phase = p.phase AND e.n_expected = p.n_sectors
WHERE p.code IN (${driver_a:sqlstring}, ${driver_b:sqlstring})
GROUP BY p.code, p.compound, p.stint, p.phase
ORDER BY p.code, p.stint, p.phase

panels.title: Compound pace across the field
panels.description: Every driver's laps pooled by compound, so the spread carries driver skill as well as tyre behaviour: read the mean as a compound comparison and the std as a reminder of that. A qualifying session usually runs one compound, which makes this a one-row-per-phase table until a race is loaded.

targets.rawSql:
WITH s AS (
    SELECT season, round, session_code FROM dim_session WHERE session_id = $session
),
sectors AS (
    SELECT microsector_id, phase
    FROM dim_microsector
    WHERE session_id = $session
      AND grain = 'corner_phase'
      AND length_m >= $min_sector_m
),
expected AS (
    SELECT phase, count(*) AS n_expected FROM sectors GROUP BY phase
),
per_lap AS (
    SELECT l.lap_id, l.code, l.compound, l.stint, sec.phase,
           sum(f.time_s) AS phase_time_s,
           count(*)      AS n_sectors
    FROM fact_microsector f
    CROSS JOIN s
    JOIN dim_lap l ON l.lap_id = f.lap_id
    JOIN sectors sec ON sec.microsector_id = f.microsector_id
    WHERE f.season = s.season AND f.round = s.round AND f.session_code = s.session_code
      AND f.grain = 'corner_phase'
      AND NOT f.partial
      AND f.time_s IS NOT NULL
      AND l.session_id = $session
    GROUP BY l.lap_id, l.code, l.compound, l.stint, sec.phase
)
SELECT p.compound, p.phase,
       count(DISTINCT p.code) AS drivers,
       count(*) AS laps,
       avg(p.phase_time_s)         AS "mean s",
       stddev_samp(p.phase_time_s) AS "std s",
       min(p.phase_time_s)         AS "best s"
FROM per_lap p
JOIN expected e ON e.phase = p.phase AND e.n_expected = p.n_sectors
GROUP BY p.compound, p.phase
ORDER BY p.phase, p.compound

list.name: session
list.label: Session
list.description: Every session loaded by F005, newest first.
list.query:
SELECT session_id AS __value,
       season || ' R' || round || ' ' || session_code || ' — ' || event_name AS __text
FROM dim_session
ORDER BY season DESC, round DESC, session_code
list.definition:
SELECT session_id AS __value,
       season || ' R' || round || ' ' || session_code || ' — ' || event_name AS __text
FROM dim_session
ORDER BY season DESC, round DESC, session_code

list.name: driver_a
list.label: Driver A
list.description: Ordered by best lap, so this defaults to the fastest driver in the session.
list.query:
SELECT code
FROM dim_lap
WHERE session_id = $session
GROUP BY code
ORDER BY min(lap_time_s) NULLS LAST
list.definition:
SELECT code
FROM dim_lap
WHERE session_id = $session
GROUP BY code
ORDER BY min(lap_time_s) NULLS LAST

list.name: driver_b
list.label: Driver B
list.description: Driver A is excluded, so this defaults to the second fastest and a lap is never compared with itself.
list.query:
SELECT code
FROM dim_lap
WHERE session_id = $session
  AND code <> ${driver_a:sqlstring}
GROUP BY code
ORDER BY min(lap_time_s) NULLS LAST
list.definition:
SELECT code
FROM dim_lap
WHERE session_id = $session
  AND code <> ${driver_a:sqlstring}
GROUP BY code
ORDER BY min(lap_time_s) NULLS LAST

list.name: lap_a
list.label: Lap A
list.description: Ordered by lap time, so this defaults to the driver's fastest lap (decision D7: the reference is a parameter).
list.query:
SELECT lap_id AS __value,
       'L' || lap_number || '  ·  '
       || coalesce(to_char(lap_time_s::numeric, 'FM990.000') || ' s', 'no time') AS __text
FROM dim_lap
WHERE session_id = $session
  AND code = ${driver_a:sqlstring}
ORDER BY lap_time_s NULLS LAST, lap_number
list.definition:
SELECT lap_id AS __value,
       'L' || lap_number || '  ·  '
       || coalesce(to_char(lap_time_s::numeric, 'FM990.000') || ' s', 'no time') AS __text
FROM dim_lap
WHERE session_id = $session
  AND code = ${driver_a:sqlstring}
ORDER BY lap_time_s NULLS LAST, lap_number

list.name: lap_b
list.label: Lap B
list.description: Ordered by lap time, so this defaults to the driver's fastest lap.
list.query:
SELECT lap_id AS __value,
       'L' || lap_number || '  ·  '
       || coalesce(to_char(lap_time_s::numeric, 'FM990.000') || ' s', 'no time') AS __text
FROM dim_lap
WHERE session_id = $session
  AND code = ${driver_b:sqlstring}
ORDER BY lap_time_s NULLS LAST, lap_number
list.definition:
SELECT lap_id AS __value,
       'L' || lap_number || '  ·  '
       || coalesce(to_char(lap_time_s::numeric, 'FM990.000') || ' s', 'no time') AS __text
FROM dim_lap
WHERE session_id = $session
  AND code = ${driver_b:sqlstring}
ORDER BY lap_time_s NULLS LAST, lap_number

list.name: min_sector_m
list.label: Shortest ranked micro-sector (m)
list.description: F004: a micro-sector shorter than about three grid bins carries more noise than signal, so it is not ranked. It is still listed in the table and still counted in the closure.

title: Pit wall — lap comparison
